answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a stake graph: each agent is a vertex whose reputation accrues only through costly, verifiable work, so spawning fake vertices costs real compute and time. Newcomers enter through a narrow inlet, a rate-limited onboarding queue with proof of work, while a haven of established, high-reputation agents vouches for them. An attacker must therefore buy many expensive, aged vertices instead of minting free identities, making a fake-identity flood uneconomic.
